title: The plan document: comments that end in decisions, live
author: pratos with Claude Code
summary: A Plan gets its document: Participants open a Thread on a Block and resolve it into a Decision that stays attached to that Block. Every tab on the Plan sees each change at once, through the PlanRoom's hibernating sockets. Resolving ships behind `resolve-thread`, checked in `decide()`.
current: cp-04 has accounts and sign-in, the Flags service with `resolve-thread` seeded off but allowlisted for admin and pratos, admin pages and Playwright. There is no Plan yet. No Durable Object, thread commands, event log per Plan or page at `/plans/:id`.
discoveries: The PlanRoom appends a command's events in one synchronous block, so `ThreadResolved` and `DecisionRecorded` land together or not at all.
Flags cross into the Durable Object as a list of names; a function would arrive as an RPC stub whose promise reads as true.
Thread commands carry `by` in the body (`CommandEnvelope`); the page's *acting as* field sets it, starting as `pratos`.
`docs/DOMAIN-VOCABULARY.md` has no `ThreadClosed` and bans *verdict*, so the vocabulary check catches the first pass by name alone.
The upcaster is a pure function tested on a verbatim v1 stream; `PlanRoom.read()` does not call it yet.
endState: Two tabs on `/plans/gh-12`: a Thread opened in one appears in the other, and resolving it shows who decided what. A first pass that calls the event `ThreadClosed` fails `just domain-vocabulary-check`, and `just review main` flags it.
notDoing: Hiding Resolve without the flag; until the release stage the page shows the refusal.
Reopening a Thread or editing a Decision; a change of mind is a new Thread.
Sessions and the agent; they arrive at cp-06.
Wiring the upcaster into `read()`; this stage proves the rung on a recorded stream.
Checking a thread command's `by` against the sign-in; sessions do that from cp-06.
approach: Domain first, because event shapes are the contract the room, page and tests read. Then the room and its API behind the flag, then the live page, then the checks that catch a wrong name.

Tab one opens a Thread, and the web Worker posts the command to the API.
The API reads the flags once and hands the room their names.
The room decides, then appends every event in one synchronous block.
It sends the new events to every open socket.
Tab two loads the PlanView again and shows the Thread without a refresh.

phases.name: Domain: Threads, Decisions and the v1 upcast
phases.goal: The thread decider turns three commands into events; resolving twice or with the flag off is refused; a v1 `DecisionRecorded` reads as v2.

changes.intent: Add Thread, Decision, PlanView and the CommandEnvelope for the three thread commands. PlanContent and PlanBody { content, edits, by?, at? }; PlanView gains body; CommandEnvelope accepts EditPlan.
Three commands, four events, and a state type where resolving twice cannot be written.

contract.code:
OpenThread    = defineCommand('OpenThread',    { blockId, by, body })
Reply         = defineCommand('Reply',         { threadId, by, body })
ResolveThread = defineCommand('ResolveThread', { threadId, by, decision })
ThreadOpened     = defineEvent('ThreadOpened',     { threadId, blockId, by, body })
ReplyPosted      = defineEvent('ReplyPosted',      { threadId, by, body })
ThreadResolved   = defineEvent('ThreadResolved',   { threadId, by })
DecisionRecorded = defineEvent('DecisionRecorded', { threadId, blockId, by, decision })
type ThreadState = { kind: 'none' } | { kind: 'open'; blockId: string } | { kind: 'resolved' }
// flag off → reject('resolve-thread is not enabled for this participant')

phases.name: PlanRoom and API: the behaviour exists, behind a flag
phases.goal: `POST /plans/:id/commands` decodes, reads flags once, and dispatches to the Plan's Durable Object; a refusal is 409 with the reason.

changes.intent: Bind `PLAN_ROOM` to the `PlanRoom` class, with SQLite storage.
One object per Plan: an `events` table in its SQLite, synchronous appends, every socket told. Socket pings are answered by the runtime (setWebSocketAutoResponse), so keep-alives never wake the room.
Add PlanRooms, the room's typed client, and Commands: decode, read flags, dispatch.

Command, PlanView, events and socket routes; `/readyz` also pings a room. Every /plans route needs a sign-in and an id of 1 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or dashes; writes are rate-limited per account; by comes from the sign-in.

contract.code:
POST /plans/:planId/commands → 201 { events } | 400 { rejected } | 409 { rejected }
GET  /plans/:planId          → PlanView
GET  /plans/:planId/events   → StoredEvent[]
GET  /plans/:planId/ws       → 101, a hibernating WebSocket
